How Many Jasprs Do I need?

To create the cleanest, healthiest air throughout your home, we recommend:

✔ 1 per bedroom

✔ 1 in the living or cooking area

✔ 1 in your home office or gym


💡 Bundle pricing available at checkout for extra savings!

What can Jaspr detect & filter?

Big particles like dust, hair, pet fur, lint, carpet fibers and large pollen.

Traps smells such as from smoke (wildfire, cooking, or cigarettes), and harmful chemical fumes (VOCs) from cleaners, paints, and furniture.

Reduces tiny particles such as fine dust, pollen, allergens, mold spores, and pet dander.

A six-month filter swap, start to finish

A REAL OWNER’S FILTER · [6] MONTHS · [PRIMARY BEDROOM]

One Jaspr Air Scrubber, one [primary bedroom] that gets cleaned every week. At six months the old filter comes out, a new one goes in, and you can see what the room’s air left behind.

One home’s filter. Yours will look different depending on your home, season and settings.

Clean surfaces don’t mean clean air.

- Outdoor air gets in through doors, windows and the small gaps every house has.

- Cooking puts fine particles into the room, even with the range hood on.

- Walking, vacuuming and the vents lift settled dust back into the air you’re in.

What are you actually looking at?

  • That gray layer is what the filter pulled out of one room’s air: dust, lint and fine particles that stay in the air long after the surfaces look clean.
  • It shows how much built up over a stated period in one real room.
  • It doesn’t show which particles they are, whether gases or odors were removed, or how anyone feels. We’d rather show you the filter and be straight about what it proves.

How Jaspr catches it.

Jaspr draws room air in and pushes it through one large, layered filter before sending it back into the room.

The pre-filter stops lint, hair and larger dust. The particle filter catches the fine particles, and it’s the layer that turns gray. 1 lb of carbon is there for odors; its work doesn’t show up as color, so we don’t use the filter to prove it.

114 CFM at fan speed 1 · 33 dBA at its lowest speed · a new filter every six months, swapped in under 30 seconds.

What this means for your lungs.

You breathe whatever is in the room’s air. A filter keeps what it catches. Your lungs get what it doesn’t.

The gray layer you saw is what Jaspr’s filter caught in one room over six months: dust, lint and fine particles that stayed in the air long after the surfaces looked clean. Every bit of it that lands on the filter is a bit that isn’t left in the air you’re breathing.

That’s the whole idea: more of it on the filter, less of it in the air, in the rooms where your family spends the most time.

A used filter can’t tell you which particles they were, or how any one person feels.
